parsed.rationale: Although both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` live in the same `Playback` package and share a handful of method names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `stop`), the structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and a null Jaccard similarity, indicating the pipeline found no formally shared slots. More importantly, the two protocols encode distinct domain responsibilities: `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` is a low-level AVAudioEngine buffer-scheduling interface (exposing `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `makeRenderTapStream`, `volume`, `play:() throws`), while `TimeShiftablePlayer` is a higher-level time-shifting playback contract (exposing `seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `isAtLiveEdge`, `stateStream`, `timePositionStream`). Forcing a parent–child inheritance relationship would couple unrelated abstraction layers and leak AVAudioEngine buffer concerns into the time-shifting contract, or vice versa. The coincidence of a few lifecycle method names (`stop`, `isPlaying`) is structural only and does not imply a shared semantic contract worth extracting.
